business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Personal Electronics and Smart Gadgets

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Korea (the Republic of Korea; national unitary jurisdiction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income
Free Trade Agreement between the Republic of Korea and the United States of America (KORUS FTA)
Free Trade Agreement between the Republic of Korea and the European Union and its Member States

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transactions Reports Act (Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, Act No. 6516, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree; Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KFIU) regulations on customer identification and beneficial ownership; the Prohibition of Financing for Offenses of Public Pressure Act; the Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended) regarding the shareholder register and corporate records. There is no public UBO register for private Chusik Hoesas; UBO information is accessible only to KFIU, National Tax Service, Korea Customs Service and other designated competent authorities. Financial institutions must identify any natural person ultimately owning or controlling at least 25% of the corporation, matching the Government_Only_Access disclosure level.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or government registrar in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive route: (a) Hague Apostille route if the issuing jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member: the local competent authority (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State, U.K. Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, Hong Kong High Court) issues an Apostille; no Korean consular legalization is added. (b) Consular legalization route only for a non-member jurisdiction: local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by legalization at the Consular Division of the Embassy/Consulate of the Republic of Korea with territorial jurisdiction; no Apostille is added.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence of each foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of companies or tax authority of the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive route: (a) Apostille route for Apostille member states: local competent authority affixes an Apostille; Korean consular legalization is not to be chained. (b) Consular legalization route for non-member states: local Ministry of Foreign Affairs certification then legalization by the Republic of Korea Embassy/Consulate with territorial jurisdiction; no Apostille is to be affixed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and/or Power of Attorney authorizing the Korean Chusik Hoesa formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of each foreign shareholder, notarized by a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive route: (a) Apostille route: the notarized resolution is completed by an Apostille issued by the competent authority of the notary's jurisdiction if an Apostille member. (b) Consular legalization route: the notarized resolution is certified by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the Korean Embassy/Consulate with territorial jurisdiction if a non-member state. Both routes must never be used simultaneously.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Charter/Statutes) of each foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent company or its official corporate records office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive route: (a) Apostille route: certified copy from registrar or notary plus Apostille by competent authority where the issuer is in a Convention state; no Korean consular service. (b) Consular legalization route: certificate of the issuing registrar or notary plus local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and Korean consular legalization where the issuer is outside the Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming source of funds and banking relationship of the ultimate beneficial owner or foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution maintaining the foreign shareholder's principal bank account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive route: (a) Apostille route if the bank is in an Apostille member state: bank signature notarized and Apostille issued by the competent authority; no Korean consular legalization. (b) Consular legalization route if the bank is in a non-member state: notarized bank signature, local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then Korean consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Government-issued identification document of each UBO and authorized signatory (passport or state-issued ID)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/ID issuing authority of the UBO's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Mutually exclusive route: (a) Apostille route for member jurisdictions: notarized copy of the ID certified by a notary and Apostilled by the competent authority; no Korean consulate step. (b) Consular legalization route for non-member jurisdictions: notarized copy, local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, and legalization by the Korean Embassy/Consulate with territorial jurisdiction.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Effective Stage 1 screening must be continuous, risk-based, and documented. The mandatory screening universe covers: (i) Korean PEP and domestic sanctions lists maintained by the FSC/KFIU and Ministry of Justice; (ii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists; (iii) United Nations Security Council consolidated lists and UN sanctions with force in Korea; (iv) EU and UK consolidated sanctions to maintain correspondent banking standards; (v) Korea's consolidated financial sanctions list; and (vi) Interpol notices, adverse media, and criminal/tax compliance databases. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for foreign PEPs, sanctioned-jurisdiction ties, or unexplained wealth. Screening results must be timestamped, refreshed within 24 hours of a sanctions-list update, and retained for at least five years after the relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office - Internet Registration Office (IRO) portal (Korean corporate name search and commercial registry records)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official corporate name of a Chusik Hoesa must be entered in the Korean registry in the Korean alphabet (Hangeul) and must include the corporate type suffix. An English or foreign-language trade name may be recorded as an external/foreign name in the filing, but the statutory registered name remains in Korean. The four-tier naming convention consists of (1) a proprietary distinctive element; (2) a business objective or trade descriptor; (3) the corporate type 'Chusik Hoesa'; and (4) an optional brand/trademark suffix. Transliteration from English to Korean must follow the phonetic adaptation of the mark into Hangeul; the registration officer will reject names that are identical, deceptively similar, or that fail to include the required corporate type suffix.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection notice, the applicant has seven days to submit a written reconsideration request to the head of the registry office, attaching the original name-search report and argument that the name is neither identical nor confusingly similar to an existing registered name and is not a regulated token. If the registry maintains the rejection, the applicant may file an immediate administrative appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act with the district court having jurisdiction over the registry office, or in parallel correct the name and file a fresh registration application. There is no statutory extension of the 30-day reservation; after expiration, the name is released and a new search and filing is compulsory.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A PO Box or pure mail-forwarding virtual office is not an acceptable registered head office for Korean tax and legal purposes. The Commercial Act requires an actual identifiable place for management, registered with the court; the National Tax Service will refuse a business registration certificate if the address is only a commercial mailbox, and Korean banks will not open an operating account for e-commerce payment rails including Stripe and PayPal without a physical business address. A serviced office or co-working lease is permissible for an online consumer-gadgets retailer provided it is a genuine business premise with a lease, signage, access, and records; the bank's AML unit will still require a compliance visit or substantial evidence of actual use.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Internal operational risk assessment: medium likelihood for online consumer-electronics retail under ISIC 4791, quantified at approximately 25%-35% within the first 12 months of registration. Checklist for an unannounced municipal tax or registry inspection: (i) visible business sign matching the registered name; (ii) a director or local staff available on site; (iii) inventory or fulfilment-centre evidence; (iv) utility bills and lease agreement in the company name; (v) bank statements corroborating VAT and sales; (vi) registered business-purpose consistency with the Internet sales platforms; and (vii) availability of accounting/statutory records at the registered office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search, trademark pre-clearance, and legal name-clearance opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (no official fee) and external Korean counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market flat fee for name-clearance and conflict search

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Court registration tax (capital registration duty) for incorporation of Chusik Hoesa
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registry Office of the district court where the Korean head office is located
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registration Fee Act / Local Tax Act: approximately 0.4% of subscribed capital; estimated on KRW 100,000,000 capital (approx. USD 300) with minimum amounts applicable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Republic of Korea National Tax Service / local government

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the Korean Articles of Incorporation and corporate formation minutes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean notary public licensed under the Notary Act
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary Act official tariff for artificial entity formation instruments

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Korean translation of foreign corporate bundle and apostille/consular legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator, apostille-issuing competent authority, or Consular Division of the Korean Embassy/Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Certified translation market rate plus statutory consular legalization fee (mutually exclusive apostille or consular route)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: National Tax Service business registration certificate for VAT and online retail
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: National Tax Service district tax office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official government fee for business registration certificate issuance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stage 1 pre-incorporation due diligence, UBO piercing, PEP/sanctions screening, and legal drafting
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Korean law firm and AML/CFT compliance counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark flat fee for foreign-investor Chusik Hoesa Stage 1 compliance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as most recently amended), restated in the Korean Government Statute Book; applicable sections: Articles 288, 289, 292, 293, 295, 300, 302, 303, 306, 308, 312, 314, 317, 365, 382, 386, and 393.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court of Korea, Internet Registration Office (iROS), and the local District Court Registry having jurisdiction over the registered office of the Company.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation with attached Articles of Incorporation; the operative record is the Corporate Registration Certificate (Commercial Register extract).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None; there is no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, under Article 295 of the Commercial Act, the full amount of the subscribed share capital must be paid into a bank or postal savings account before the incorporation application is filed, and the deposit may not be withdrawn unless the incorporation is denied or the Company is legally registered; the deposit is then released to the representative director.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [CLIENT COMPANY] CHUSIK HOESA, ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS ON [DATE] AT [REGISTERED OFFICE]. WHEREAS, the Company has been incorporated as a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and holds corporate registration certificate number [NR]; WHEREAS, the Board of Directors has the authority to manage the affairs of the Company under the Articles of Incorporation and Article 393 of the Commercial Act; WHEREAS, the Company aims to operate an online retail business selling personal electronics and smart gadgets under ISIC 4791; WHEREAS, the Board must establish the corporate basis for banking, statutory representation, and governance before commencing operations. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. Share Capital Subscription. The issued and paid-up share capital of the Company has been subscribed in full by the shareholders whose names appear in the capital subscription ledger. Each share has been fully paid into the Company's capital deposit account. The directors are instructed to ensure that the capital subscription ledger, share allotment lists, and the subscribers' ledgers are kept current and are made available to the registry and auditors upon demand. 2. Banking Authorization. The directors hereby establish the Company's principal banking relationship with [Korea Bank Name] at the branch [Branch Name, Address]. The Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, if any, are each authorized severally, and the CEO and CFO jointly, to open, operate, and close deposit and foreign currency accounts, issue withdrawal instructions, execute electronic banking mandate agreements, and provide signature cards and corporate authorization documents to the bank. 3. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [Address, District, Seoul/Republic of Korea]. This address shall be used for the delivery of legal notices, statutory communications, and all filings with the Supreme Court registry, the National Tax Service, and transactional counterparties. The directors are directed to update the corporate register if the office is ever relocated. 4. Officers. The following persons are elected and appointed: [Name], Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name], Director; and [Name], Auditor, if applicable. The Representative Director shall have full power to represent the Company in court and before all administrative organs and to execute contracts in the ordinary course of business. The directors adopt the corporate seal and agree to keep the seal and seal certificate in secure custody. 5. Implementation. The Corporate Secretary is instructed to execute all documents and payments required to complete the registration of this resolution, to open all tax filings, and to submit the mail-order seller report to the relevant local administrative authority before the first sale is transacted. This Resolution is effective as of its adoption and may be signed by all directors in unanimous written consent, without a physically assembled meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Association notaries and the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (iROS) for company name verification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation setting out the corporate name ending with Chusik Hoesa, the precise objects for online retail of personal electronics and smart gadgets, the amount of authorized share capital, the number and class of shares, the method of convening shareholder meetings, the number of directors and auditor, the term of the Company, the method of public notices, and the registered office address. Execute the Articles before a notary public who will identify the incorporators and certify that the instrument complies with Articles 289 and 292 of the Commercial Act. Confirm through iROS that the proposed corporate name does not conflict with an existing registered entity and does not contain prohibited terms. Notarial fees and stamp duty are paid at this stage, and the notarized Articles become the foundational constitutional instrument for the incorporation registration.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity of each incorporator
Proposed business scope and project authorization documents
Corporate name search result from iROS
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies non-mandatory provisions or the iROS namecheck reports similarity, amend the Articles of Incorporation and re-execute them within 3 business days; the only administrative refusal available at this stage is a company name conflict, and the remedy is to adopt an alternative name and proceed with a fresh notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription of Shares and Paid-in Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank incorporated under the Banking Act of South Korea, including KB Kookmin, Shinhan, Hana, Woori, or NH Nonghyup Bank; no government registry is involved at this step.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters or the sole shareholder shall subscribe to all issued shares and transfer the full amount of the subscription price to a bank deposit account opened for the incorporation. Under Article 295 of the Commercial Act, the funds must be paid into the bank before the court application for registration. Retain the original deposit certificate showing the depositor, the corporate name, the account number, and the amount deposited. The deposit may be claimed only after the Company is incorporated by the representative director, except where the incorporation application is denied, in which case the subscribers may reclaim the funds. Prepare a capital subscription report listing subscribers, number of shares, and amount paid, and keep all payment transfer records for the registry and the future auditor.
required_dossiers: Bank deposit certificate for the entire subscription price
List of subscribers with shares and amounts
Capital subscription agreement and payment transfer receipts
Executed Articles of Incorporation and incorporators' identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue a deposit certificate because of anti-money laundering queries, supply source-of-funds evidence or correct the account name to match the Articles of Incorporation exactly, then re-apply to the bank within 2 business days; the incorporation must not proceed without a valid deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Appointment of Directors and Statutory Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders of the Company acting as the constituent shareholders' meeting; the resulting minutes and acceptance letters are later reviewed by the District Court Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a constituent shareholders' meeting or obtain unanimous written consent of all incorporators to ratify the Articles of Incorporation, elect directors and an auditor if the Company exceeds the statutory exemption threshold, and appoint the representative director. Adopt the meeting minutes in Korean and, if required, notarize them for registration purposes. Receive from each director and auditor a written acceptance of office and confirm the term of office. Verify the external audit exemption: under Article 8 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Company with paid-in capital below KRW 10 billion may dispense with a statutory auditor; if the Company does not reach that threshold, no auditor needs to be appointed, but the sole director, if any, may also become the representative director.
required_dossiers: Written resolutions of the organizational meeting in Korean
Notice convening the meeting and attendance sheet
Written acceptance letters of directors and auditor, if any
Consent form waiving statutory auditor if the exemption applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry later questions the external audit exemption due to miscalculation of paid-in capital, submit a unanimous shareholder waiver or appoint a suitable auditor through a corrective filing within 5 business days; if the appointment process is defective, re-convene a general meeting and file supplemental minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Incorporation Registration through iROS and the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (iROS, iros.go.kr) and the local District Court Registry with jurisdiction over the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the incorporation registration application in Korean through iROS or file in writing with the district court civil registry. The application must be submitted within two weeks after the whole amount of the initial share capital has been deposited into the bank. Upload or attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital deposit certificate, the minutes of the organizational meeting, the written acceptance letters of directors and auditor, the corporate seal specimen card, and proof of payment of the court registration fee and education tax. The registry examiner verifies compliance with the Commercial Act and, upon approval, issues the Corporate Registration Certificate. The Company is legally incorporated as of the registration date, and the representative director must immediately obtain a corporate seal certificate for subsequent business registrations.
required_dossiers: Final notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit balance certificate
Organizational meeting minutes and directors' acceptance letters
Corporate seal specimen and seal registration card application
Proof of payment of court registration fee and education tax
Power of attorney or authorization for the filing agent, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementary order or correction directive, cure the identified defects within the stated statutory period, usually 5 business days, and upload the corrected document through iROS; if the application is rejected, file an immediate administrative appeal or objection with the district court within 1 week from receipt of the rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Mail-Order Seller Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through Home Tax (hometax.go.kr), and the local si/gun/gu administrative authority for the mail-order seller report under Article 12 of the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, Etc.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Corporate Registration Certificate, file business registration with the competent tax office within 20 days of business commencement. The NTS will issue a business registration certificate containing the corporate tax number and VAT registration. Before commencing online sales, submit the mail-order seller report to the local administrative authority, stating the online mall name, URL, corporate details, and facility location. This is a mandatory pre-operational report for online retail under ISIC 4791, although it is not an industrial operating license. The representative director must also open a corporate bank account, order a corporate seal certificate, and register the entity as a merchant with Stripe and PayPal as the target payment rails, submitting standard entity documentation and bank account verification to each processor.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporate Registration
Business registration application form
Certificate of registered corporate seal and corporate seal impression
Lease or ownership document of the registered office
Mail-order seller report form
Identity cards or passports of the representative director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office assesses a penalty for late business registration, request a penalty reduction by proving unavoidable circumstances and file the corrective registration within 14 days of notice; if the mail-order seller report is returned because the URL or office address is incomplete or inconsistent, correct the particulars and re-submit, and the local administrative authority must issue the confirmation without further substantive requirements within 5 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable; no industrial licensing board is engaged for ISIC 4791 online retail of personal electronics and smart gadgets; the local si/gun/gu administrative authority handles only the mail-order seller report.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable as a statutory industrial operating license; however, before online sales begin, the Company must file a Mail-Order Seller Report under Article 12 of the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, Etc. with the local government.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; the Ministry of Environment and the Korea Environment Corporation (KECO) have no jurisdiction over pure online retail operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable; ISIC 4791 online retail is not listed as an activity requiring Full Environmental Impact Assessment, Prior Environmental Review, or Environmental Registration under the Korean Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; the Company will not operate a point source, emit VOCs, discharge wastewater, or handle hazardous waste; therefore no permits under the Clean Air Conservation Act, Water Environment Conservation Act, or Wastes Control Act are required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for the pure digital retail operation. If the Company uses a leased office, the building owner's fire safety certificate and comprehensive property insurance satisfy Civil Defense requirements; if the Company later opens a warehouse or physical assembly facility, it must obtain a Civil Defense fire safety permit, undergo structural load inspection, and register the workplace under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr). Cross-border goods clearance and export validation are administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through its electronic portal UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Confirm the Korean tax nexus: a Chusik Hoesa is a resident corporation and must register for Korean corporation tax and VAT. A foreign non-resident entity selling consumer electronics through online retail should register a Korean permanent establishment/place of business if it maintains an office, warehouse, employees or dependent agents in Korea. If no Korean fixed place of business exists but the entity makes digital/electronic service supplies to Korean customers, it must obtain a Business Registration Number through the NTS foreign business registration procedure and appoint a Korean tax representative. For cross-border physical goods exports to Korean buyers with no Korean PE, import VAT is normally accounted for by the Korean buyer/importer at customs, and the foreign seller is not automatically required to register. 2. File the statutory Business Registration Application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business, or file online through HomeTax via an authorized representative. 3. Supporting documents for a foreign legal entity include: apostilled certificate of incorporation and corporate existence, certified Korean translation, articles of association, board resolution resolving the establishment of the Korean place of business and appointing the tax representative, power of attorney, proof of local office or warehouse lease or ownership, passport/ID copy of the representative, and the foreign business registration certificate. 4. After receiving the Business Registration Number, register with the Korea Customs Service in UNI-PASS to obtain the unique importer/exporter code required for export declarations and import clearance. 5. The NTS issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which simultaneously serves as the corporate tax identification number and VAT registration number; it must be displayed on e-tax invoices and customs declarations and must be updated within statutory timeframes upon any change of address, business scope or representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election. The Chusik Hoesa is automatically taxable at the corporate entity level. A qualifying parent company and its wholly-owned Korean subsidiaries may elect the Korean consolidated corporation tax filing regime, but this election does not alter indirect tax classification or create pass-through treatment for VAT; no hybrid mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for VAT registration. Any person or business making taxable supplies in Korea must file Business Registration within 20 days of commencement, and foreign suppliers of electronic services are also required to register regardless of amount. The simplified taxpayer turnover threshold of KRW 80 million per year is an administrative simplification for very small businesses and is not a VAT registration exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT tax invoices in Korea must be issued as Electronic Tax Invoices (ETIs) through the NTS HomeTax e-tax invoice system or through an NTS-certified ASP connected to HomeTax by application program interfaces. Each ETI is transmitted to the NTS at the time of issuance and given a national electronic document number; anti-fraud checks monitor duplicate invoices, abnormal B2B chains and mismatched returns. The zero-rated export status must be shown on the ETI. Goods imported for online retail resale must be reported to the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS, and import VAT is collected at customs clearance before release; properly documented input VAT can be credited against output VAT on the subsequent domestic retail sale.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating is available under VAT Act Article 21 when goods are supplied to a foreign purchaser and physically exported from South Korea under a customs export procedure. The seller must maintain contemporaneous proof of shipment, delivery terms and foreign exchange receipt. Qualifying offshore digital services are zero-rated only when supplied to a foreign non-resident recipient; sale of consumer electronics to Korean consumers or delivery to a Korean address is a domestic supply subject to 10% VAT, not export zero-rating. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated export sales may be refunded after being claimed in the VAT return through HomeTax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS, evidencing customs clearance of the goods
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier
Electronic Tax Invoice for the zero-rated export, issued through NTS HomeTax where applicable

Foreign exchange bank confirmation/certificate of export proceeds received, or equivalent bank records showing repatriation of the export sale value within the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act deadline
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS audits retrospectively compare customs export records, e-tax invoices, VAT returns and foreign exchange receipts. If zero-rating is claimed without complete export and proceeds documentation, NTS may deny the zero rate, assess 10% VAT on the supply, add statutory daily overdue surcharges, impose administrative understatement penalties and, for fraudulent or intentionally concealed transactions, refer the case for criminal prosecution. The standard re-assessment limitation period is five years, extended to ten years for cases involving intentional omission or international tax fraud; clawback may therefore cover all open prior periods with cumulative interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act enforcement framework, administered through licensed foreign exchange banks and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a largely liberalized current-account foreign exchange regime. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act permits trade-related payments to be cleared and converted into KRW without pre-approval, but requires every regulated transaction to be routed through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions, including equity injections, intra-group loans, and profit repatriation, are permitted under a declaration-and-capture model rather than a strict licensing model, provided the remitting bank receives accurate FEIS reporting. In practice, dividends to non-resident shareholders are treated as current-account remittances only after the bank verifies tax clearance, audited financial statements, and shareholder meeting resolutions. There is no mandatory central surrender requirement for export proceeds; exporters may hold foreign currency domestically and convert at their own discretion. The primary conversion risk is therefore not government denial but documentary mismatches, late FEIS declarations, unexplained source-of-wealth gaps, and mismatched purpose codes, which can trigger BOK-oriented bank compliance holds and materially delay KRW clearing. For this Chusik Hoesa engaged in online consumer electronics retail, full convertibility is achievable only through one principal Korean foreign exchange bank that maintains the entity's entire FX ledger, corporate account, and trade file, thereby creating a transparent audit trail for all inward and outward flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and current Korean bank operating regulations, export proceeds must be received through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank within six months from the export declaration date, unless the bank approves a formal extension. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio for proceeds; the directive is zero percent mandatory conversion, meaning 100 percent of export receipts may be retained in a foreign currency domestic account for future hedging or overseas disbursement. Any export payment not collected within the six-month statutory window must be supported by a written justification and documentary evidence of collection delay; conventional electronic goods orders with extended buyer payment terms are regularly accepted as long as the bank files the relevant FEIS extension notice.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account and KRW settlement clearing account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI licenses do not convey authority to perform foreign exchange intermediation or bank-facing settlement within the Republic of Korea under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Korean banks will not accept an unlicensed fintech EMI as the primary clearing rail for statutory capital verification, corporate billings, or FEIS reporting. A foreign EMI may be used only as a customer-side payment acquisition gateway where its underlying funds eventually settle into a licensed Korean bank account; it cannot replace a tier-one domestic commercial bank for corporate treasury execution, regulatory reporting, or FX conversion. For this consumer electronics retail Chusik Hoesa, the bank onboarding blueprint must therefore designate a single licensed Korean foreign exchange bank as the exclusive liquidity clearing intermediary.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one authorized director, senior officer, or qualifying beneficial owner with a notarized board resolution must physically attend the in-branch KYC interview at the chosen Korean foreign exchange bank. Remote mobile onboarding may be accepted if the final beneficial owner already holds a Korean Certified Digital Certificate and the bank's digital onboarding system verifies the Real-Name Financial System, but a consular proxy is permitted only for document legalization, not as a substitute for the live underwriting interview. The presenting individual must bring the original Certificate of Business Registration, corporate seal certificate, shareholder register, board resolutions, passport, and proof of the capital contributor's bank relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner with initial capital funding sourced from opaque private wealth or untraceable third-party payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide 12 months of personal and corporate bank statements from the shareholder's home jurisdiction, source-jurisdiction tax clearance certificates, a certified audit opinion on the contributing company, notarized passport copies, the Chusik Hoesa shareholder register, a board resolution approving the capital contribution, and a CFO wealth-sourcing letter explaining accumulated operating profits applicable to the capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial equity remittance arriving from a digital-asset exchange, money service business, or unrelated personal account rather than the direct shareholder corporate account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a fully traced remittance chain from the ultimate operating bank account to the Korean receiving bank, certified board resolution identifying the remitter and the exact equity subscription amount, signed subscription agreement, underlying commercial invoices or audited profit statements supporting each source leg, custodian bank references, and a declaration that no virtual asset exchange or MSB was involved in the transfer path.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Declared online consumer electronics retail scope but transaction velocity or counterparty profile inconsistent with low-risk e-commerce operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver Korea Customs Service export declarations, import/export licenses, master purchasing agreements, supplier registration documents, electrical goods conformity certificates, three months of transaction-level bank statements, shipping logs, and a payment matching matrix aligning every invoice with a corresponding SWIFT MT103 or trade finance instrument.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-EMI treasury fragmentation, third-party FX bookings, or unexplained cross-border disbursements across non-Korean settlement platforms
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execute and evidence a treasury consolidation plan: signed board resolution cancelling all external EMI clearing agreements, a single-bank mandate designating the Korean foreign exchange bank as exclusive treasury counterparty, an itemized trail of all prior FX transactions, proof that each legacy payment was ultimately cleared through a licensed Korean bank, and an external audit confirmation that no unlicensed EMI balance remains outstanding.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All equity capital must enter through a direct SWIFT MT103 wire from the non-resident shareholder's corporate banking account to the designated Korean foreign exchange bank escrow account. The wire instruction must name the Korean Chusik Hoesa as the receiver, identify the remitter as the shareholder, and contain a purpose description stating direct equity investment contribution under Article 6 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Before execution, the beneficial owner or legal counsel must confirm whether the contribution triggers Foreign Investment Promotion Act reporting thresholds, and if so, file the required foreign direct investment declaration with the designated bank or Korean Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) portal. Upon maturity of the wire, the receiving bank issues the Foreign Currency Deposit Certificate and the foreign exchange sale contract at the prevailing bank rate when converting to KRW. The statutory capital verification package consists of the CPA positive bank confirmation, the foreign currency capital receipt, the FX conversion certificate, the FEIS filing confirmation, and the board meeting book evidencing resolution and share issuance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The Korean Chusik Hoesa should clear all supplier and trade disbursements through SWIFT MT103 for direct US dollar or euro supplier wires, using explicit payment purpose entries aligned with the local foreign exchange bank's FEIS reporting format. For larger consumer electronics procurement orders, issue a commercial letter of credit under MT700 from the principal Korean bank, and use documentary collections with INCOTERMS for established repeat suppliers when full LC formality would be inefficient. Every international disbursement exceeding the bank's statutory declaration threshold must be reported through FEIS, and the bank will not execute the payment if the beneficiary bank appears on the terrorism financing, money laundering, or international sanctions list. Trade settlement records must be maintained against the corresponding customs declaration and supplier invoice so the bank can satisfy cross-border trade transparency requirements on audit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forward contracts with the licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, strictly tied to verified trade receivables or payables with a documented inventory procurement exposure
FX options purchased from the licensed Korean bank for KRW/USD hedging on confirmed electronics import orders, prohibiting speculative uncovered option writing
Cross-currency swap (CCS) agreements between USD and KRW to hedge intra-group funding facilities and long-term trade credit lines

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) instruments are not permissible for ordinary onshore corporate hedging by a Korean Chusik Hoesa; any offshore NDF must be transacted by foreign counterparties only and cannot be booked through the Korean entity's treasury ledger

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Act, Article 60; return form including final financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Home Tax Service (HTS) at the district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year fiscal year ending December 31, by March 31 of the next year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surtax of 10% of the final corporate tax liability (20% if the delinquency exceeds six months), a 0.022% daily interest charge for underpayment, possible tax seizure and assignment of receivables, and after persistent non-compliance the NTS may administratively cancel the business registration and request court dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Surtax Return (Local Tax Act, local income tax surcharge on corporate income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the municipality (si, gun, gu) through the WeATIS integrated local tax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the national corporate tax return deadline; for a calendar-year company, by April 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax delinquency surcharge at 0.66% per month for the first 3 months and 0.75% per month thereafter; prolonged non-payment can trigger forced collection, seizure of bank deposits and moveable assets, and cancellation of business registration by the competent district tax office

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent Auditors' Report and Audited Financial Statements (Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Article 5)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and, for designated public-interest companies, the DART electronic disclosure system; audited accounts are also submitted to shareholders at the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: When the mandate is triggered, the audited financial statements and audit report must be presented to the annual general meeting no later than 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, by March 31 of the following year, with the report also delivered to FSS under the external audit filing procedures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or to file the audit report exposes the company and representative director to administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000 (about USD 35,700) and adverse FSS enforcement disclosure; repeated omissions can lead to criminal prosecution and disqualification of directors, but do not by themselves trigger administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register of Shareholders Update / Share Transfer Record Maintenance and Non-Resident Foreign Investment Status Confirmation (if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained at the registered office; change notifications are filed with the registry court and, in the case of non-resident holdings, with a foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual public filing is due for a private unlisted Chusik Hoesa; share transfers must be recorded in the register within 30 days of the transfer, changes of directors or the representative director must be filed at the registry court within 14 days of the shareholders' meeting, and non-resident investors must report acquisitions or transfers to the foreign exchange bank within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Regulatory fines of up to KRW 10,000,000 for failure to maintain statutory books; false or postponed registration can result in refusal of shareholder rights and administrative fines; inaccurate foreign investment reports trigger fines up to KRW 20,000,000 and may temporarily block dividend remittance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent Certified CPA audit is triggered for a Chusik Hoesa if, at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, any of the following is true: (a) total assets on the balance sheet exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 8,570,000); (b) annual sales revenue exceeds KRW 10,000,000,000 (approximately USD 7,140,000); (c) the company is a listed issuer, financial institution, securities firm, or other public-interest entity designated by the Financial Supervisory Service; (d) the company is part of a large business group subject to the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act and is not eligible for the small-company exemption under the Enforcement Decree of the External Audit Act. Banks and payment processors may contractually require an external audit earlier than the statutory threshold under internal AML and credit policies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Listed and designated public-interest entities must prepare statutory financial statements under K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards, substantively identical to IFRS). A private unlisted Chusik Hoesa may elect either K-IFRS or K-GAAP as codified by the Korea Accounting Standards Board, but the chosen framework must be applied consistently, and the external auditor's report must conform to the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not require a standalone annual UBO declaration to a public registry for a private unlisted Chusik Hoesa. Instead, the shareholders' register is conclusive; transfers of shares are effective only upon entry and any transfer must be recorded within 30 days. Non-resident foreign investors must additionally report acquisitions or disposals of shares to a foreign exchange bank, and through it to the Ministry of Economy and Finance, within 30 days under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Annually, the company must maintain the statutory registers at its registered office and produce them to the NTS, FSS, or court on demand. Banks and financial institutions conducting periodic AML/KYC reviews may request a confirmation of the current ultimate beneficial owner, and the company should respond to such confirmation annually or whenever a triggering event occurs.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders' register) including all classes, transfers, names, and holdings
Register of Directors and statutory auditor (if any) including appointment and removal records
Register of Charges, mortgages, and encumbrances over company assets
Minute Book of shareholders' general meetings and board of directors' meetings
Corporate seal usage log and registered office corporate records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,000 to USD 2,500 per annum for a registered office and corporate secretarial agent arrangement in Seoul
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 to USD 18,000 per engagement for a small or mid-sized unlisted consumer electronics e-commerce company, plus VAT; higher if cross-border intra-group balances or complex inventories are involved

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (base 10% for first KRW 200 million; 20% for next KRW 200 million; 22% for next KRW 200 million; 24% for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surtax on the national corporate tax, yielding a combined statutory headline rate of 26.4% on the highest bracket)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax holidays for new growth engine industries; 50%–100% reduction for venture startups in designated technology business; special tax credits for R&D (up to 30–50% of qualifying expenditure); foreign-invested enterprise tax reductions under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (RSTA); no separate patent box, but IP income may benefit from R&D tax credit and technology transfer income exemption (50%–100% for certain qualifying transfers)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (법인세법 제60조; Form No. 1 or 2) filed via HomeTax (홈택스) electronic system; consolidated filing includes the national corporate income tax return and the local income tax surcharge return (지방소득세 특별징수)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (interim/prepayments are semi-annual: August 31 and December 31 for fiscal-year taxpayers; final return due within 3 months after fiscal year-end)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final corporate tax return must be filed within 3 months from the end of the fiscal year (Article 60(1) of the Corporate Income Tax Act). For a December 31 fiscal year-end, the filing deadline is March 31 of the following year. An extension of up to 1 month is available (Article 67(1) of the Enforcement Decree) for entities with foreign transactions, or upon application with justifiable cause.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 — Business Registration Number and Company Identification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the 10-digit business registration number (사업자등록번호), legal entity name, head office address, representative director name, fiscal year-end date, and business classification code (KSIC code, typically 4791 for online retail).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and foreign directors need not be listed in Box 1, but the local filing agent or representative (국내사업장) must be identified. If the entity is a foreign investment company under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, indicate the foreign investment ratio and the relevant Foreign Investment Notification number; cross-border e-commerce operators must ensure the local place of effective management (POEM) is clearly disclosed to avoid dual-residency claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 — Financial Statements Reconciliation (损益调整)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report book net income before tax as per Korean GAAP or K-IFRS financial statements. Reconcile to taxable income by adding non-deductible expenses (e.g., entertainment expense exceedance, fines, bribes) and subtracting non-taxable income (e.g., dividend received deduction, technology transfer income exemption).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to related foreign entities (e.g., imported goods, royalties, service fees) must be scrutinized for transfer pricing adjustments. Any understatement of revenue from online retail sales to Korean customers must be reversed if the sales were sourced to Korea; foreign currency translation gains/losses must be booked in accordance with K-IFRS 1217/1021. The tax return must be filed in Korean won (KRW) and the exchange rate must be the base exchange rate on the transaction date or the year-end closing rate as prescribed by the Enforcement Decree.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the taxable income after applying loss carryforwards, exemption deductions (e.g., venture startup tax reduction), and non-taxable income adjustments. Show the final taxable income breakdown across the progressive brackets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned chusik hoesa, ensure that any interest on loans from foreign shareholders exceeding the thin capitalization safe harbor (debt-equity ratio 2:1 for general companies, 3:1 for financial institutions) is disallowed as interest expense and reclassified as constructive dividend. Also confirm that no deduction is claimed for royalties paid to a foreign related party unless the technology was actually used in Korea and the rate is arm's length under the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 — Tax Calculation and Credits (산출세액 및 세액공제)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the national corporate income tax using the progressive rates, then subtract applicable tax credits (R&D credits, employment credits, foreign tax credits, temporary investment tax credits). Compute the local income tax surcharge (10% of national corporate tax).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits may be claimed for income taxes paid overseas on the same income, but the credit is capped at the Korean tax attributable to that foreign-source income (Article 57 of the Corporate Income Tax Act). For cross-border e-commerce income, only income effectively connected to a Korean business establishment (고정사업장) is taxable; if the foreign headquarters concludes sales contracts and performs customer support outside Korea, no Korean PE should be recognized, but the domestic corporation must substantiate its separate legal existence to avoid PE attribution of profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 — Taxable Income after Deduction of Tax Credits (차감납부세액)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Arrive at the final national tax payable after credits, and the local income tax surcharge payable. Indicate any advance payments (중간예납) already made and the amount of tax still due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company is a foreign-invested enterprise with a tax reduction under Article 121.2 of the RSTA, attach the applicable tax reduction certificate. For non-resident shareholders, withholding tax on dividends must be separately remitted in the shareholder dividend withholding return. The tax payable must be paid by the filing deadline; extension of filing does not extend the payment deadline unless a specialized payment deferral is approved by the local tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 — Attached Schedules and Transfer Pricing Disclosures (첨부명세서)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach statutory schedules including the statement of adjustment of taxable income (조정명세서), financial statements, tax reconciliation of entertainment expenses, and the Local File / Master File if thresholds are met. Disclose all intercompany transactions with foreign related parties (e.g., sales of goods, service fees, royalty payments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Two critical schedules apply: Schedule 1 on related-party transactions (특수관계인 거래명세서) and Schedule 2 on international tax adjustment (국제조세조정명세서). A non-resident entity with cross-border payments must state the TP method applied, the arm's length price range, and the OECD TNMM or CUP benchmarks. Failing to disclose a reportable transaction is itself a penalty of up to 3% of the transaction amount or KRW 100 million (Article 8 of the International Tax Adjustment Act).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 20% of the underpaid tax if filed after the statutory deadline (up to KRW 300 million for corporations with total assets above KRW 5 billion; flat 1% per month for other cases). Late payment surcharge: 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum) on unpaid tax. Negligence penalty: 10% of understated tax for general underreporting, 20% for false invoices; 30% for omissions of related-party transactions. Fraudulent evasion triggers criminal referral under Article 118 of the Corporate Income Tax Act: imprisonment up to 5 years or fine up to 3 times the evaded tax. For repeated offenders, imprisonment up to 10 years and additional financial penalty. Corporate veil cannot shield the representative director or tax officer who signs the return; statutory representation clauses and labor law incremental penalties apply.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (15% national tax plus 10% local surtax on the national tax, equivalent to 16.5% national plus 1.5% local = 18% for most? Let's accurately state: The national withholding tax on dividends is 15% under the Corporate Income Tax Act / Personal Income Tax Act for resident individuals, but for non-resident corporations it is 20% (Article 98-1 of the Corporate Income Tax Act). A 10% local income tax surtax is imposed on the national tax, bringing the combined statutory WHT for non-resident corporate shareholders to 22% (20% national + 2% local, as 10% of 20% = 2%).)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced rate under a Korean Double Tax Treaty (e.g., Korea–USA, Korea–Hong Kong, Korea–Singapore), the non-resident shareholder must submit: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate (거주자증명서) issued by the competent authority of the residence country, stamped with apostille or consular legalization if required; (2) a Certificate of Beneficial Ownership (실질귀속자 확인서) signed by the ultimate beneficial owner, attesting that they are not a conduit; (3) an application for treaty relief on withholding tax (외국법인 조세조약 특례 신청서) to the Korean withholding agent (the local company) before the payment date or within the statutory period for refund (generally 3 years from the end of the year in which the tax was withheld). The local company must report the payment and the treaty reduction on a separate statement attached to the withholding return. If the beneficial ownership is not proven (e.g., the shareholder is a shell entity without economic substance in the residence country), the withholding tax rate reverts to the statutory 22% and additional collection of unpaid tax plus penalties may be imposed. The National Tax Service (NTS) applies the 'substance-over-form' principle; a LOB (Limitation on Benefits) clause in many Korean treaties may deny treaty benefits unless the shareholder meets a 'derivative benefits' test or is listed on a recognized stock exchange.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest 22% (20% national + 2% local surtax); royalties 22% (20% national + 2% local surtax). Treaty rates vary by country: e.g., under the Korea–USA treaty, interest 10%, royalties 10%; under the Korea–Hong Kong treaty, interest 10%, royalties 10%; under the Korea–China treaty, interest 10%, royalties 10%; under the Korea–Japan treaty, interest 10%, royalties 10%. All treaty reductions require the same TRC and beneficial ownership documentation. Interest paid to a foreign related party may be denied entirely if deemed excessive under the thin capitalization rule (debt-to-equity ratio of 2:1); royalties must be at arm's length under the International Tax Adjustment Act Article 5, and if the payee has no economic substance, the royalty may be recharacterized as a dividend and lose the treaty rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File must be prepared if both (i) the total intercompany transaction value with foreign related parties exceeds KRW 100 billion (approximately USD 75 million) in the fiscal year, or (ii) the company's total revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion. However, for the purpose of all tax filings, a transaction-by-transaction disclosure is required for any related-party transaction above KRW 500 million. A simplified Local File is sufficient if the intercompany transactions are below KRW 5 billion but the company fails the exemption threshold. On request, the NTS can impose a penalty of up to KRW 30 million for non-submission of TP documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies the OECD Principal Purpose Test (PPT) and GAAR under the Framework Convention for the Prevention of Tax Treaty Abuse. The economic substance doctrine requires that a Korean resident company (chusik hoesa) maintains a real office, employees, and actual decision-making power for its core income-generating activities (CIGA), particularly for e-commerce operations such as logistics, customer service, marketing, and order fulfillment. Korean domestic law does not have a formal 'Economic Substance Regulations' (ESR) like the UAE, but the NTS applies substance-over-form under Article 15 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and the LOB/PPT provisions of tax treaties. If the Korean entity is a mere shell with no management and non-resident directors control all its functions, the NTS may disregard the local entity's separate existence and attribute its income to the foreign headquarters, exposing the foreign parent to Korean branch taxation and filing penalties. For digital platform businesses, the new 'Offline VAT' and 'Online Purchase Tax' initiatives do not require extra corporate substance, but the Indian, Korean, and other Asian tax authorities increasingly demand evidence of core functions in the jurisdiction where risks and assets are located.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Arm's Length Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean chusik hoesa sells consumer electronics on its own online store and imports the same products from its Hong Kong or Singapore related party at a transfer price that yields a net operating margin of less than 3%, while the Korean entity bears the full inventory and market risks. The taxpayer fails to prepare, retain, and produce a Local File and Master File within 60 days of the NTS request, despite intercompany purchases exceeding KRW 50 billion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 11 and 15 of the International Tax Adjustment Act (국제조세조정에관한법률): the NTS may adjust the taxable income to reflect the arm's length price and impose an understatement penalty of 30% of the resulting additional tax (or 10% if the taxpayer reported in good faith but with insufficient documentation). Additionally, a separate documentation penalty of up to KRW 100 million applies for failure to submit the required TP files. If the adjustment is made through a deemed dividend to the foreign shareholder, withholding tax at 22% (or treaty rate) is collected, increasing the effective cash cost.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director (대표이사) is personally liable for the unpaid corporate taxes and penalties if the NTS proves that the director intentionally or negligently omitted the TP documentation and thereby caused the tax loss. Under Article 38 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, a director who approves the filing of a false corporate tax return is jointly liable with the corporation for the tax, interest, and penalties up to the amount of the corporation's assets that the director diverted or disposed of with intent to evade the tax. In flagrant cases, the NTS may file a criminal complaint under Article 118 of the Corporate Income Tax Act (조세범 처벌법) for 'tax avoidance by fraudulent means', carrying imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to 5 times the evaded tax. Directors may also be blacklisted from board positions in financial institutions for 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company without Economic Substance (PE Trigger and Treaty Abuse)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity is registered as a chusik hoesa with a registered office address that is a virtual office; it has zero employees, no physical inventory, and all day-to-day management is performed by executives in Japan/China through remote control. The Korean entity invoices all e-commerce sales to Korean customers, but the ownership, risks, and strategic functions are managed by the foreign parent, and the local company does not exercise any entrepreneurial control. The company claims the benefit of the Korea-Japan DTA to exempt its service income from Japanese tax, but a Japanese tax audit reveals that the Korean entity is a letterbox company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS may apply the 'substance-over-form' principle under Article 15 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and the OECD's Principal Purpose Test to deny the DTA benefit, treating the Korean entity as a permanent establishment of the foreign parent. This results in reassessment of the Korean source income tax (normal corporate tax plus 10% local surcharge), plus 40% penalty for 'serious negligence' under Article 35 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, and withholding tax on the deemed dividend to the foreign parent. The foreign parent may also lose treaty benefits on all future payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The nominee directors of the Korean shell company are personally liable for the tax claims if they signed the corporate tax return while knowing the company had no real operations; they can be jointly assessed under Article 39 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. Criminal sanctions under the Aggravated Punishment Act for Specific Economic Crimes (특정경제범죄 가중처벌법) apply if the tax evasion amount exceeds KRW 300 million—imprisonment of 3 to 20 years and a fine equal to 2 to 5 times the evaded amount. A travel ban (출국금지) may be imposed on the directors while the criminal investigation is pending, and they may be subject to overseas asset tracing and extradition under the Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty with the relevant jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Dividend and Royalty Taxes at Source (WHT Evasion)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean chusik hoesa declares and pays a dividend to its foreign parent without withholding the statutory 22% (or treaty-reduced 10–15%) WHT, or it remits royalty payments to a related offshore IP company in a zero-tax jurisdiction without any documentation, intentionally failing to withhold. It also fails to file the monthly withholding return (원천징수이행상황신고) with the NTS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 98(1) of the Corporate Income Tax Act: the payer must withhold and pay the tax to the tax office by the 10th day of the following month. Failure to withhold carries a penalty of 10% of the uncollected amount plus daily surcharge of 0.022% on the unpaid amount. The foreign payee remains liable for the tax, and the local company is not relieved from obligation; the NTS may collect the WHT from the local company as a responsible taxpayer. A refund claim by the foreign shareholder will require the withholding agent to amend the withholding return and pay the full statutory tax, plus penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the board of directors (이사회) resolves to make a dividend distribution without arranging for WHT, each director who voted in favor is personally and severally liable for the uncollected WHT, penalties, and interest under Articles 67 and 68 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. The NTS commonly pursues claims against the assets of directors (including personal bank accounts, real estate) via asset seizure (압류) and garnishment (추심). Criminal indictment under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (조세범 처벌법 제3조): imprisonment up to 2 years or a fine up to 2 times the unpaid tax; if the undeclared withholding tax exceeds KRW 100 million, imprisonment up to 5 years. Additionally, the foreign parent may be considered a 'second debtor' and the Korean government may demand payment from its Korean subsidiary's directors personally in cross-border bankruptcy proceedings.
